headline: High: shared writable workspace and allowlisted egress in B create medium-to-high risks for leakage and cascading errors; A is non-runnable but can still seed unsafe content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is non-runnable and has no I/O surfaces, so it cannot directly inject B. However, B reads/writes files and its skills reference each other on shared context, so if A’s content is copied into B’s workspace, B may treat it as trusted instructions. The pathway is indirect but plausible.
conditions: IF A-generated text is copied into a file under B's skill paths, B may parse it as instructions.
IF B is configured to consume shared-context files without provenance checks, prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of B's skill directories.
Add a provenance header to any copied content.
Review B inputs before execution.
Use separate workspaces for A and B.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filtering to B.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B reads files and can call external APIs with allowlisted egress. If sensitive material is placed in shared files, B can ingest and transmit it to GitHub or marketing-skills.com. The pairwise leakage path is therefore present in default B workflows.
conditions: IF sensitive data is stored in files readable by B, B can load it.
IF B sends those file-derived contents to its allowed APIs, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Store sensitive files outside B's readable paths.
Disable API calls for runs handling sensitive data.
Use a separate non-shared workspace.
Redact secrets before B reads files.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention on B's file inputs and API outputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. B can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, and supports multiple instances, so concurrent B runs can conflict with each other on shared files. The pair itself is not symmetric, but the interaction still creates write contention if A’s artifacts are placed in B’s workspace.
conditions: IF two B instances operate on the same writable directory, file conflicts can occur.
IF A artifacts are copied into B's writable workspace, B may overwrite or race on them.
mitigations: Run only one B instance per workspace.
Use per-run directories.
Lock shared files before writes.
Keep A artifacts read-only.
requires-engineering: add workspace locking to B.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a curated list and not runnable, so it does not generate operational facts itself. But B’s skills build on shared context, meaning copied A content can become authoritative input for B’s marketing outputs. Without verification, B may propagate stale or irrelevant recommendations derived from A’s list structure.
conditions: IF A-derived content is used as source material for B outputs, B may treat it as authoritative.
IF B lacks a verification step for copied context, errors can cascade into published marketing content.
mitigations: Verify A-derived claims before reuse.
Mark copied content as untrusted.
Require human review for B outputs.
Limit B to fresh sources only.
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates to B.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data classes are identified for A, and B only lists marketing content/product marketing context. The main compliance issue is documentation quality: A is verified docs-only, while B is docs-only but unverified. That is a gap, but not a residency or regulated-data breach on the provided profiles.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent's workflow, compliance risk may increase.
IF B is used for retention-sensitive marketing records, policy mismatch could matter.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in both agents.
Document retention rules for B.
Review B's unverified docs before deployment.
Separate marketing content from sensitive records.
requires-engineering: add formal compliance mapping for B.
